SSC Photo and Signature Size

For SSC exams such as CGL, CHSL, MTS and GD, the application asks for a signature and, depending on the notice, a photograph. Use the presets below to prepare each file.

Size ranges last reviewed: 2026-10-04. Always confirm against your exam notification.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Exam range: Targets sit a little below the maximum. Check your notice.
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

What SSC asks for

Requirements change with every notification. The ranges on this page are figures commonly reported for recent 2026 notices by exam-preparation websites, and the sources do not always agree. We have not verified them against each official PDF, so always follow the notification or instructions on the official application portal for your exam.

Reports of recent SSC CGL and CHSL 2026 notices describe a signature in JPEG format of about 10–20 KB, and a photograph of about 20–50 KB where a photo file is uploaded. They also describe live photograph capture during the application for those exams, so you may not upload a photo file at all. Pixel sizes quoted by different websites vary, which is one more reason to read the notice itself.

Prepare the signature

Sign on plain white paper with a black pen, in your usual style and not in capital letters unless the notice says so. Photograph or scan it in even light, with no shadows, and crop around the signature with a small margin. Then choose the Signature 10–20 KB preset here, add the file, and download the result. The preset aims for about 19 KB so it stays under the 20 KB limit.

Prepare the photograph

If your exam uses an uploaded photo, use a recent colour photograph with a plain light background and your face clearly visible, cropped to passport framing. Choose the Photo 20–50 KB preset. The target is 47 KB, which keeps a margin below 50 KB.

Why the targets are below the limit

A file of 20.2 KB on a 20 KB portal can fail the upload. This site counts 1KB as 1,024 bytes, and some portals count 1,000 bytes, so the presets leave a margin instead of aiming exactly at the limit.

If the signature is too small

A signature on white paper can compress to a few KB, which may fall under the 10 KB minimum. The tool warns you when this happens. Photograph the signature larger, use a thicker pen, or crop less tightly so more pixels are encoded, then try again.

Common reasons for rejection

Typical problems are a wrong file format (such as a PNG renamed to JPG), a file outside the size range, a blurry or faint signature, a photo with a dark or busy background, and a mismatch with the live photo. Check each item before you upload.

Related help

Read the guide to general photo and signature sizes, or the blog post on why a portal says the file is too large after you compressed it.

Quick checklist

Before uploading, confirm the notice you are following is for your exam and year, the signature is dark and readable, the file is a genuine JPEG, the size is inside the range, and you have kept the original photograph and scan. If something fails, change one thing at a time and try again.

Common questions

Does SSC accept PNG?

Exam notices usually ask for JPEG or JPG. Convert with JPEG output here and check the downloaded file ends in .jpg.

Are the pixel sizes the same for every SSC exam?

Not necessarily. Sources differ, so use the dimensions in your own notice and crop first if a specific shape is needed.
